item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 012327
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Tue Sep 1 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, on Hurricane Lowell, located several hundred
miles southeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm
Marie, located several hundred miles southwest of southwestern
Mexico.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of Mexico over the
weekend. Gradual development is possible early next week as the
system moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, and is likely
to remain well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Marie are issued under WMO
header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Marie are issued under WMO
header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Kelly

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 18.3 North, longitude 130.8 West. Karina is moving
toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h) and a westward to
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 140 mph (220 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Gradual weakening is expected 
during the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 946 mb (27.94 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 020238
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Tue Sep 01 2026
 
The infrared satellite presentation for Karina has improved over
the last several hours as the cloud tops have cooled down to around
-70 degrees Celsius. Based on the presentation from the infrared 
and analysis from the SHIP guidance, Karina has developed annular 
characteristics. However, the eye still remains cloud filled at
this time. The current satellite intensity estimates range from
114 to 129 kt. Therefore, the initial intensity for this advisory 
has been brought up to 120 kt.
 
The major hurricane is moving westward at about 9 kt. A general
slow westward to west-northwestward motion is expected during the
next 3 to 4 days as a narrow mid-level ridge remains situated to the
north of the hurricane. During the weekend, a turn to the northwest
seems likely as the ridge shifts eastward and the cyclone 
approaches a mid- to upper-level low north of Hawaii.  The current 
NHC forecast track is very similiar to the previous one with 
only small adjustments in speed and is slightly to the right 
of the previous track. The current official forecast track 
continues to keep the hurricane to the north of the Hawaiian 
Islands. 

In the short term, the hurricane has the opportunity to intensify a 
bit, however, in the long run, the environment will become less 
favorable for Karina due to cooler ocean waters and decreasing 
relative humidity. With Karina developing annular characteristics 
the rate of weakening is expected to be slower at first. The current 
NHC intensity forecast shows a bit of strengthening within the first 
12 h, and then a gradual weakening for 24 to 60h. Past 60 h, the 
rate of weakening should increase as the low- to mid-level relative 
humidity drops below 40%.

...MARIE STRENGTHENS SOME MORE...
...EXPECTED TO BECOME A HURRICANE ON WEDNESDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.1N 110.3W
ABOUT 470 MI...755 KM S OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was 
located near latitude 16.1 North, longitude 110.3 West. Marie is 
moving toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn toward the 
west-northwest is expected on Wednesday and that motion should 
continue through Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 65 mph (100 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Additional strengthening is expected during the 
next few days, and Marie is expected to become a hurricane on 
Wednesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
few days and will likely spread northward to southern California
over the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 020235
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM MST Tue Sep 01 2026
 
The satellite presentation for Marie continues to improve this 
evening, with the low-level center beneath deep convection with 
cold cloud tops near -80C. Satellite intensity estimates have also 
increased, with the latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from 
TAFB T3.5/55 kt. Objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range 
from 37 to 55 kt. Based on the improving satellite trends and these 
estimates, the initial intensity is raised to 55kt.

The initial motion is northwestward, or 310/8 kt. This motion is 
expected to continue for the next day or so as Marie rounds the 
western periphery of a mid-level ridge over Mexico. The ridge is 
then forecast to build to the north of the system, which should 
cause Marie to gradually turn toward the west-northwest. Beyond 72 
hours, track uncertainty increases as an amplifying trough along the 
U.S. West Coast is forecast to cause the system to slow down. While 
there is less confidence in the track late in the forecast period, 
the latest NHC forecast continues to lie near the reliable HCCA and 
GDMI consensus aids with a more westward track.
 
Marie is moving over warm sea surface temperatures and will remain 
in a low vertical wind shear environment for the next couple of 
days. The system remains fairly broad, but steady strengthening is 
anticipated once the structure becomes better organized. Some of the 
latest SHIPS rapid intensification guidance is around a 50 percent 
chance of RI in the next 24 h. The new NHC intensity forecast is 
similar to the previous one and closely follows the trends of the 
HCCA and IVCN consensus aids, although does not explicitly call for 
rapid intensification. Some guidance shows a faster rate of 
strengthening, though this remains heavily dependent on how quickly 
the system's structure improves. Toward the end of the forecast 
period, Marie is forecast to move over cooler SSTs and into a drier, 
more stable air mass, which should induce a gradual weakening 
trend.
